PlatformProgressionTrack.description: A ladder of ranks in one discipline that the organization uses. Reference the `id` as `progressionTrackId` on a program to make the sessions of its class types count toward these ranks.

sport.description: Canonical sport id the ladder belongs to, e.g. "jiu-jitsu".

custom.description: True for the organization's own track, or its copy of a template; false for a global template.

enabled.description: Whether the organization uses it: always for its own tracks, and for a template once enabled.

levelCount.description: How many ranks the ladder has.

classTypeIds.description: Class types whose sessions count toward this track: those of its programs. Empty means every session counts; once any is linked, only sessions of the linked types do.

PlatformProgressionLevel.description: One rank on a progression track.

level.description: The step within the rank when the discipline has one, e.g. "3rd Dan"; usually empty.

name.description: `skill` and `level` together, as the dashboard shows them.

requiredSessions.description: Sessions a member attends at the rank below before they are eligible for this one.

requiredDays.description: Days a member holds the rank below before they are eligible for this one.

ageOutLevelId.description: The rank members continue at on the track this one ages out onto; that track's first rank when null.

maxStripes.description: Most stripes a member earns within a rank; 0 when the discipline has none.

ageOutAge.description: The age at which members continue on `ageOutTrackId`.

templateId.description: The global template this track was copied from.

PlatformProgressionLevelWrite.description: A level in a saved ladder. With `id` an existing level is kept and only the fields sent change; without, a new one is added and `skill` is required.

enabled.description: For a global template only, and the only field it takes: start or stop using it.

ageOutTrackId.description: Another track the organization uses, that members continue on at `ageOutAge`.

levels.description: The whole ladder, lowest rank first. A level left out is removed.

PlatformProgressionTrackCreate.description: A new track needs `name` and `sport`; a copy of a template needs only `fromTemplateId`.

fromTemplateId.description: A global template to copy into the organization's own. Not with `levels`.

PlatformPromotionProgress.description: How close a member is to the next rank, against each requirement it sets. Null at the track's top rank, or when the next rank sets no requirement.

sessions.description: Sessions attended since the current rank was earned.

days.description: Days at the current rank, on the club's clock.

learnedItems.description: Skills of the next rank's curriculum learned.

eligible.description: Every requirement the next rank sets is met. A signal only: the rank changes when staff give it.

earnedOn.description: The calendar date the rank was earned.

total.description: Total members matching the filters, ignoring pagination

ranks.description: The current rank on each track the organization uses.

timeline.description: Every rank and stripe recorded, latest earned first.

levelId.description: The rank to give, a level of this track.

next.description: True for each member's own next rank, stripes back to zero.

stripes.description: Stripes at `levelId`, up to the track's `maxStripes`.

earnedOn.description: The calendar date it was earned; today when omitted. May be in the past.

notifyMember.description: Tell the member about a move forward. False when recording ranks they already hold.

skipped.description: Left as they were by `next`: no rank on the track to move up from, or already at its top.

failed.description: Failed; everyone else was still ranked.

PlatformInstructorType.description: A kind of coach the organization has. Reference the `id` as `instructorTypeId` on an instructor. One shape for the list, get-by-id, create and update.

slug.description: Stable key, derived from the name when a create does not send one. A rename never moves it.

sortOrder.description: Position in the order staff set in Settings, 1 first. Lists come back in this order; change it with the type's PUT .../order.

revenueAccountId.description: Where a session with a coach of this kind posts. Null falls back to the organization's default account.

instructorCount.description: Coaches currently filed under this type, active and retired.

maxConcurrentBookings.description: How many one-to-one sessions a coach of this kind may hold in the same slot. What a booking is actually checked against is the instructor's own value; this is the shape of the type, not an override.

maxPlayers.description: How many people one session with a coach of this kind may bring, the person booking included. 1 is one-to-one. A session with them and no area may be booked for any group up to this; a session on an area takes the area's own player limit instead.

PlatformTypeOrder.description: A new order for the organization's instructor, class or area types.

orderedIds.description: The type ids, first to last. A type left out keeps its place after the listed ones.

PlatformContactAudience.description: Who something applies to, as a set of predicates a contact must match. `null` means everybody. The same shape a promotion segment and an automation entry condition use. `membershipPlanIds` is which plan the contact must HOLD, not which plan a purchase discounts.

tags.description: Tag ids or names the contact carries.

membershipPlanIds.description: Membership plans the contact must hold, from GET /v1/platform/plans.

membershipPlanCategoryIds.description: Plan categories the contact must hold a plan in.

progressionLevelIds.description: Progression levels the contact must hold, each counting that level or above on its track: "blue belt and up". The contact's current rank is its latest earned one.

PlatformPayRatePolicyEarnings.description: What the coach earns, and for what unit of work. `kind` decides which of the rate fields apply and which are rejected: an `individual` policy takes `perSession`, `perAdditionalPlayer` and `sessionRevenuePercentage`, a `class` policy takes `perClass`, `perBooking` and `classRevenuePercentage`. At least one of the applicable rates must be greater than zero, and `kind` cannot be changed once the policy exists.

perSession.description: Individual policies: a flat amount for each private session.

perAdditionalPlayer.description: Individual policies: added to `perSession` for each person beyond the first in the group a session with no area was booked for (see the instructor type `maxPlayers`). A one-to-one session earns nothing from it.

sessionRevenuePercentage.description: Individual policies: a share of what the session took (see `sessionRevenueBase`).

sessionRevenueBase.description: Individual policies: what `sessionRevenuePercentage` is a share of. `session` (the default) is the whole session's price, court included. `coach_charge` is only the coach's own charge - the coach half of a court booked with a coach - so 100% pays a coach exactly the fee the member paid for them. Left out of an update, it stays as it was.

perClass.description: Class policies: a flat amount for running the class at all.

perBooking.description: Class policies: a flat amount for each attendee.

classRevenuePercentage.description: Class policies: a share of what the class took.

PlatformPayRateEntranceScope.description: One way an attendee got in, narrowing what a policy pays for. `membershipPlanId` applies only to `membership`, and `externalProgramId` only to `external_program`; sending the wrong pairing is a 400.

membershipPlanId.description: Narrow to one membership plan, from GET /v1/platform/plans.

PlatformPayRatePolicy.description: A rule for what the club pays a coach. Not an instructor's `hourlyRate`, which is what a member pays for an hour of their time. Each coverage list means "everything" when empty: no `instructors` makes it the organization default, no `classTypes` covers every class type, no `entranceScopes` covers every way in.

instructors.description: Coaches this policy covers. Empty means every coach with no policy of their own.

classTypes.description: Class types it covers. Empty means every class type.

entranceScopes.description: How the attendee got in. Empty means every route in.

PlatformPayRatePolicyCreate.description: Fields accepted when creating a pay rate policy. `instructorIds` must be present: an empty list is the organization default and applies to every coach without a policy of their own, so it has to be asked for rather than fallen into. The other coverage lists mean "everything" when omitted.

requirePaidBooking.description: When true, attendance that was never paid for earns the coach nothing.

instructorIds.description: Coaches this policy covers. An empty list makes it the organization default, applying to every coach with no policy of their own.

classTypeIds.description: Class types it covers, from GET /v1/platform/class-types. Empty covers every class type. Rejected on an `individual` policy, which has no classes to scope.

entranceScopes.description: How the attendee got in. Empty covers every route in.

PlatformPayRatePolicyUpdate.description: Fields accepted when updating a pay rate policy. Send only what changes; an omitted field is left alone, and any list that IS sent replaces the whole set. `earnings.kind` must match the policy's existing kind.

requirePaidBooking.description: When true, attendance that was never paid for earns the coach nothing.

instructorIds.description: Coaches this policy covers. An empty list makes it the organization default, applying to every coach with no policy of their own.

classTypeIds.description: Class types it covers, from GET /v1/platform/class-types. Empty covers every class type. Rejected on an `individual` policy, which has no classes to scope.

entranceScopes.description: How the attendee got in. Empty covers every route in.

PlatformPayLedgerLine.description: One unit of work a coach is paid for - a private session, a class, or an attendee of a class - and what it paid under the coach's pay rate policy. `pending` is work the paid-booking gate is holding back: `totalAmount` is what it will pay once the member settles, and nothing is owed yet.

revenueBase.description: What the work took, before the coach was paid - the base a revenue percentage applies to.

components.description: How `totalAmount` was reached: each rate that applied and what it added.

startTime.description: Wall-clock `HH:mm` on a template; an ISO instant on a shift.

PlatformShiftTemplate.description: A named shift a roster is built from, on the wall clock of the club it is worked at.

clubId.description: Null means every club of the organization.

PlatformShiftTemplateWrite.description: A shift template. On create `name`, `startTime` and `endTime` are required; on update send only what changes, and `breaks`, when sent, replaces the whole set.

weekIndex.description: Zero-based week of the cycle, below `cycleWeeks`.

shiftTemplateId.description: The shift worked that day. Null, or a day with no slot, is a day off.

PlatformShiftRotation.description: A weekly pattern of shifts, one to twelve weeks long, that coaches are assigned to.

anchorDate.description: The first day of week 1 of the cycle.

PlatformShiftRotationWrite.description: A rotation. On create `name` and `cycleWeeks` are required; on update send only what changes, and `slots`, when sent, replaces the whole pattern.

anchorDate.description: First day of week 1. Defaults to today.

PlatformShiftRotationAssignment.description: A coach on a rotation over a range of days.

cycleOffset.description: Zero-based week of the cycle the coach starts on.

generated.description: Shifts materialized on the staff roster by this write.

PlatformInstructorShift.description: One shift on the staff roster: when a coach works on one day. This is what their availability reads.

date.description: The day the shift starts on, on the club clock.

isOverride.description: Edited by hand: regenerating the rotation leaves it as it is.

PlatformInstructorTimeOff.description: A window a coach cannot be booked in, whatever their staff roster says.

PlatformInstructorTimeOffConflict.description: A booking or class already on the coach diary inside a time-off window. Time off leaves it in place.

id.description: The booking id, or the class id.

seasonId.description: Set on a week of a contracted Season Slot, which is moved to another coach rather than cancelled.

PlatformPlanCategory.description: How membership plans are grouped - the headings on a price list and the sections of a plans page.

sortOrder.description: Ascending display order; ties fall back to name.

planCount.description: Membership plans currently in this category, active and retired.

PlatformRevenueAccount.description: One account in the organization's chart of accounts. Reference the `id` as `revenueAccountId` on a membership plan, a product, a class type, an area type or an instructor type to decide where its sales post.

code.description: The chart-of-accounts code, which is how the club's bookkeeper names the account. Unique within the organization.

isActive.description: False for an account retired from the chart. Still valid on existing rows; do not attach it to something new. Never false on the default.

isDefault.description: Where a sale posts when nothing on the item names an account. Exactly one account holds it, and it is always active.

PlatformRevenueAccountCreate.description: Fields accepted when creating a revenue account. `name` and `code` are required, and the code must be free within the organization. Unknown fields are rejected. The billing entity an account belongs to is not settable here - it is inherited, and re-pointing one rewrites who is selling.

code.description: The bookkeeper's code for the account, e.g. "4000". Unique within the organization; a clash is a 409.

isActive.description: False retires the account. Everything already pointing at it keeps pointing at it; there is no delete. Refused for any request that would leave the default inactive - including the first account in an empty chart, which is always made the default.

isDefault.description: Where a sale posts when the item names no account. Setting it true moves the default off whichever account currently holds it, in the same transaction and behind a per-organization lock. Ignored when the chart has no default yet - the first account always takes it, since creating one is the only way to give the organization a default. The default must be active, so anything landing an inactive one is refused.

PlatformRevenueAccountUpdate.description: Fields accepted when updating a revenue account. Send only what changes; an omitted field is left alone, and at least one is required. `isDefault: false` is refused only when this is the last account holding the default, or when the only other one is retired: the organization must be left with an active default. An organization carrying more than one default - possible from before this rule, or from a clone - can have the extras cleared, which is how that state is repaired.

code.description: The bookkeeper's code for the account, e.g. "4000". Unique within the organization; a clash is a 409.

PlatformClubProfileUpdate.description: Fields of a club's profile. Send only what changes; at least one is required. Text fields take null to clear. Unknown fields are rejected.

gettingThere.description: How to reach the club, in the club's own words - parking, the nearest stop and station. Plain text; line breaks are kept. Shown on the club's website page.

description.description: Plain text; each blank-line-separated paragraph becomes a paragraph

timezone.description: IANA timezone, e.g. `Europe/Sofia`. Derived from the address when the address changes and this is not sent.

operatingHours.description: Opening hours by lower-case weekday; a day left out keeps its hours.

status.description: `inactive` hides the club from members while staff keep running it

modified.description: True when the organization changed the role from 1club's default

permissions.description: Everything the role may do, as `module.action.scope`

catalog.description: The permissions a role can be given, by module

userCount.description: How many people have the role

modified.description: True when any of the role's categories differs from 1club's default

isConfigured.description: False while the organization keeps the default

overriddenUserCount.description: People in the role whose own choice outranks this default

name.description: The field key, which a value is addressed by

visibility.description: `Private`: staff only. Otherwise members see and edit it in the portal.

appliesTo.description: At sign-up: asked of the account holder, of each family member, or both

contactTypes.description: The contact types it applies to; empty means every contact

PlatformCustomFieldWrite.description: A contact custom field. `name` and `type` are required on create; on update send only what changes. Unknown fields are rejected.

type.description: `manual`: put on by people. `system`: a smart tag, applied from the smart tag rules. `interest`: applied from what a person books.

contactCount.description: How many contacts carry it now

PlatformTagWrite.description: A manual tag. `name` is required on create; on update send only what changes.

PlatformSmartTagSettings.description: The smart tag rules, by category. Each tagged category is `{ enabled, tags: [{ id, name, color, ...threshold }] }`; `engagement` (attendance) also carries the `period` in days its tiers count visits over; `interest` is `{ enabled, minBookings }`; `scoring` is `{ enabled }`, switching on the engagement score, which is read from visits over the attendance period. On a PATCH, send only the categories that change.

PlatformPaymentMethod.description: One of the organization's own payment methods - a tender staff record by hand, such as cash or a bank transfer.

code.description: How reports and imports name the method. Unique within the organization.

visibility.description: `Private`: staff only (the till, check-in). `Member_only` and `Public`: also offered to members paying for a booking.

PlatformPaymentMethodCreate.description: Fields accepted when creating a payment method. Unknown fields are rejected.

name.description: What staff and members see, e.g. "Bank transfer"

code.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores. Derived from the name when omitted on create. Must be free within the organization.

visibility.description: Who may choose it. Defaults to `Private` (staff only) on create.

PlatformPaymentMethodUpdate.description: Fields accepted when updating a payment method. Send only what changes; at least one field is required.

name.description: What staff and members see, e.g. "Bank transfer"

code.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores. Derived from the name when omitted on create. Must be free within the organization.

visibility.description: Who may choose it. Defaults to `Private` (staff only) on create.

PlatformMemberAccount.description: A household or company account: the family or employer a group of contacts belongs to, which an invoice can be addressed to.

type.description: `organization` is a legacy type: it is listed, but not created here.

primaryContactId.description: The member the account is addressed to by default

total.description: Total accounts matching the filters, ignoring pagination

PlatformMemberAccountCreate.description: Fields accepted when creating an account. Unknown fields are rejected.

name.description: Required for a company. A household without one is named after its first member.

contactId.description: The first member, who becomes the primary contact

role.description: The first member's role. Defaults to owner for a household and employee for a company.

PlatformMemberAccountUpdate.description: Fields accepted when updating an account. Send only what changes; at least one field is required.

primaryContactId.description: Must already be a member of the account

PlatformProductCategory.description: How products are grouped - the tabs on the till and the sections of a shop page.

sortOrder.description: Ascending display order; ties fall back to name.

productCount.description: Products currently in this category, active and inactive.

PlatformCheckin.description: An attendance record for a booking, class, membership, or direct gym visit.

total.description: Total check-ins matching the filters, ignoring pagination

PlatformInvoiceTotals.description: Invoices in one currency, added up. Amounts in different currencies are never summed together.

timezone.description: The organization's timezone, whose calendar days the range is read on

invoiced.description: One entry per currency; void and cancelled invoices excluded. Empty when nothing was invoiced.

byStatus.description: Every status present in the range, per currency, void and cancelled included

overdue.description: Unpaid invoices in the range whose due date has passed, per currency

byBillingEntity.description: `invoiced`, split by the billing entity that issued each invoice

PlatformInvoice.description: A fiscal invoice. Pro-formas are never returned.

invoiceDate.description: The calendar day the invoice belongs to, on the organization's clock

overdue.description: Unpaid and past its due date

total.description: Total invoices matching the filters, ignoring pagination

PlatformPricingRuleScope.description: A set of resources the rule prices. `areas`, `instructors`, `clubs` and `classTypes` name ids of that kind, all in this organization. A rule with several scopes applies to a booking any of them covers.

PlatformPricingRuleCondition.description: One condition a booking must meet for the rule to apply. Weekday names are lowercase English; times are 24-hour HH:mm in the club timezone (`24:00` ends a window at midnight); dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

oneOf.description: A time-of-day window, optionally on certain weekdays. By default (`match: segment`) it is a price band: the booking is split at its edges and only the part inside is priced by the rule. `start` applies the rule to the whole booking when it starts inside the window; `within` only when it fits entirely inside. Send startTime and endTime together, and name weekdays, a window, or both. A window cannot run past midnight.

weekdays.description: Days the window applies on. Empty or omitted means every day.

endTime.description: Exclusive: a slot starting at endTime is outside the window.

oneOf.description: The booking starts on one of these weekdays.
The whole booking is at least `threshold` hours long, and at most `maxThreshold` when sent. Equal values name one exact length.
A session with a coach and no court is booked for between `min` and `max` people (inclusive). The rule then prices the group as a whole. A court or class always counts as one.
The booking falls between these dates, inclusive. Send either bound or both.
A member rate: the person booking holds one of these membership plans. A walk-in with no plan never matches.
The court is booked together with a coach - one of these, or any coach when the list is empty or omitted. Pair it with an `areas` scope.

Who the booking is for: the contact matches this audience - carries one of `tags`, is one of `memberTypes`, and so on (every list sent must match). Name at least one. Creates a booking on an area (e.g. a padel court), optionally with an instructor leading the session, or with an instructor alone and no area (a private lesson where no court is booked) - send `areaId`, `instructorId`, or both. A booking with no area is placed at the instructor's club; for an instructor who works across clubs, name it with `clubId` (it can be left out when the organization has one club, and is refused with `CLUB_REQUIRED` when it has several). Identify the customer with `contactId` (resolve it via GET /v1/platform/contacts) or, for callers that do not track 1club ids, with an inline `customer` matched to a contact by email and created if new - exactly one of the two.

A booking transaction is recorded so the booking counts for revenue: `paid` marks it settled against a payment method named after your API key (no gateway call), so the club can see and reconcile what you collected separately from every other channel; `unpaid` leaves it outstanding. `amount` is the price the customer paid for the booking, before any fee you kept, and defaults to the computed price for the slot - the area's price, plus the instructor's hourly rate when one is attached. With `unpaid` and no `amount`, the booking is paid for the way the club's own staff would default it: a membership of the customer's that covers it is used (one session is spent and nothing is owed), and otherwise the price is recorded as owed. With an API key that needs the customer named by `contactId`: an inline `customer` is matched by an email anyone can type, so it never spends a membership and the price is recorded as owed. Send your own payment id as `payment.reference` and your commission as `payment.fee`: the sale is recorded at `amount`, and the fee is what the club reconciles against your payout statement.

This API assumes the calling system enforces its own booking rules, so 1club's member-facing policy (minimum notice, maximum days in advance, operating-hours envelope, slots that have already ended, instructor availability) is not applied - which is what lets an existing schedule be recorded as-is.

What the club physically has is never overridden, and a booking that breaks one of these is refused with `400` and a populated `details.conflicts[]`: the area's concurrency capacity (`AREA_AT_CAPACITY`), a court the club has blocked for maintenance or a private hire (`AREA_BLOCKED`), the instructor already booked or teaching (`INSTRUCTOR_AT_CAPACITY`, `INSTRUCTOR_TEACHING_CLASS`), whether an instructor takes one-on-one bookings, and the slot alignment the area requires. A live event on the court or run by the instructor takes one of their places, so it counts toward `AREA_AT_CAPACITY` and `INSTRUCTOR_AT_CAPACITY` and is listed in `details.conflicts[]` with `subject: event`. There is no override parameter: a conflict is a refusal, not a warning.

get.description:
Returns bookings that overlap the requested window - including one that started before `from` and is still running - ordered by start time. Each bound is an ISO date-time, or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` read as midnight UTC. When `from`/`to` are omitted the window defaults to the next 7 days, and passing one derives the other.

A single request may span at most 93 days. To cover a longer range, walk it in consecutive windows of 93 days or less, paging each window with `limit`/`offset` against the `total` it reports. A booking running across the boundary between two windows is returned by both, so de-duplicate by `id` when combining them. Ordering is stable (`startTime`, then id), so paging is well defined for a window that is not being written to; bookings created or cancelled mid-walk can still shift rows across page boundaries.

Bookings from every channel are returned, each tagged with `source`. That is deliberate: a caller reconciling its own writes has to be able to see member- and staff-created bookings to know whether a slot was already taken. Whether the writes (cancel, add/remove participant) reach those bookings too depends on the credential: an API key may only mutate the bookings it created (`source: api`), while a staff member acting through an authorized 1club assistant may mutate any of the organization's.

A class booking carries the occurrence it attends as `classId`. Every attendee of a class holds their own booking row against the same `classId`, and `classes` rows are per-occurrence, so that is what tells two groups running in the same hour apart - filter by it, or read the roster from the class side with GET /v1/platform/classes/{id}/bookings.

post.description:
Cancels the booking by its 1club id. Idempotent: cancelling an already-cancelled booking succeeds.

Which bookings are cancellable depends on the credential. An API key may cancel only the bookings it created (`source: api`); anything else is reported as not found. A staff member acting through an authorized 1club assistant may cancel any of the organization's bookings, as they can in the admin portal.

Refunds follow the money. On a booking this API created, 1club never held the payment, so it moves none - but it records what you gave back, so the club's revenue matches yours. Cancelling with an API key records a refund of everything collected unless `refund.amount` says otherwise: send the amount you actually returned to keep a cancellation fee, or `0` if you kept it all, and your own refund id as `refund.reference`. Over a staff credential nothing is recorded unless `refund` is sent. On a booking taken through 1club (member portal, app, front desk), the club is the one cancelling: an unpaid booking owes nothing unless `keepCancellationCharge` is true. A paid booking the cancellation policy would keep money from needs an explicit `keepCancellationCharge` - `false` refunds it in full, `true` applies the policy - and without one the call is refused (409 `CANCELLATION_CHARGE_DECISION_REQUIRED`), exactly as the admin portal asks. `refund` is ignored there.

A class enrolment or an event registration made with guests (POST /v1/platform/classes/{id}/bookings, POST /v1/platform/events/{id}/bookings) is one purchase: cancelling any of its seats cancels all of them, and `refund.amount` is what came back for the whole registration, recorded across its seats in proportion to what each was paid.

A booking that has already been checked in cannot be cancelled (409) - voiding a check-in is an admin-portal action. One occurrence of a recurring booking is cancelled, not the series.

Defaults to off for a booking this API created, since callers normally send their own notice, and to on for a booking taken through 1club, whose customer expects to hear it from the club. The club's own staff alerts are sent either way.

keepCancellationCharge.description: On a booking taken through 1club: `true` applies the club's cancellation policy, so a late cancellation keeps its charge; `false` refunds what was paid in full and forgives the rest. Left out, an unpaid booking owes nothing, and a paid one the policy would keep money from is refused with 409 `CANCELLATION_CHARGE_DECISION_REQUIRED`. Ignored on a booking this API created.

Its charges and cancellation records are deleted with it, and so are its players, check-ins, the instructor's pay for it and the door access it granted. It cannot be undone.

Refused with `409 BOOKING_HAS_PAYMENTS` while any of its charges was paid or has a payment, invoice, Wallet movement or refund behind it: cancel it and refund instead, so the sale stays in the books. Refused with `409 BOOKING_ON_OPEN_ORDER` (or `409 CHARGE_ON_OPEN_ORDER`) while an open order still holds it or one of its charges, and one seat of a registration with guests with `409 BOOKING_HAS_SEATS` until the registration is cancelled. Charges recorded on its check-ins count as its own. A visit it drew from a pass, the organizer's or a player's, goes back on the pass unless it was cancelled, and its External Program usages are deleted with it. An API key may delete only bookings made through the API, and never one another key manages (`409 BOOKING_EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`). For a member of staff, it needs the Extended level of booking delete, which only admins hold by default.

patch.description:
Edits a booking by its 1club id: reschedule it, move it to another area, attach or remove an instructor, reassign the contact, change its notes or price, or make it recur. Send only the fields that change. Reaches the same bookings as cancel: an API key only those it created, a staff member through an authorized 1club assistant any of the organization's.

The edit follows the admin portal's rules. A cancelled booking is final, and a booking on a class takes its time and price from the class. As on create, the club's member-facing policy (operating hours, instructor availability) is not applied, but an occupied or blocked court, or a coach who is already booked, is refused with `details.conflicts[]`.

Money follows the edit. `amount` reprices the booking to your figure. Without it, a booking this API created keeps its price, and a booking taken through 1club is re-quoted when the slot, area, instructor or contact changes. The charge is then reconciled: an increase on a paid booking leaves the difference outstanding, and a decrease below what was paid needs a refund, which this endpoint does not perform. Payment status cannot be changed here.

Recurring bookings. `recurrence` on a one-off booking makes it the first occurrence of a series. On an occurrence of a series, `scope=all_future` applies the edit to every occurrence that has not started yet, from the earliest upcoming one: a new `startTime`/`endTime` gives each that time of day on its own date (the weekday changes only through `recurrence.daysOfWeek`), a new area or instructor is checked against every date, and a new `recurrence` rewrites the cadence or end condition; days dropped from a weekly pattern are cancelled with their refund. A series bound to a recurring class follows the class and cannot be re-timed, and a booking an API key created cannot be made to recur at all (`RECURRENCE_NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_MANAGING_KEY`): 1club would be generating occurrences that key never created, so each one is its own booking. An edit whose series has already run touches nothing.

To record the visit against a zero-fee external program instead, send `externalProgramId`. The membership must not be limited to particular classes, areas or instructors, must have sessions left, and must have nothing owed on it - a member who owes is checked in at the front desk, where staff can see the balance. Creates a class. Times must be ISO 8601 instants with an explicit offset. Supports the `Idempotency-Key` header.

Without `recurrence` this creates one occurrence. With it, one request creates the whole repeating series - do not call this once per week. `startTime`/`endTime` stay required either way: they are the template slot, giving every occurrence its time of day and its duration, and the series starts from `startTime` (so there is no separate start date). A weekly rule whose `daysOfWeek` do not include that day puts the first occurrence on the first listed day at or after it.

A bounded series (`ends.type` of `until` or `after`) is materialized in full inside this request, so it is capped at 520 occurrences - over that the request is refused with `RECURRENCE_TOO_MANY_OCCURRENCES` rather than silently truncated. An open-ended series (`ends` omitted, or `ends.type: "never"`) materializes a rolling window and extends itself, so only the first weeks exist immediately.

`ends.occurrences` counts **occurrences, not weeks**, across every day in `daysOfWeek` - twelve weeks of a Monday-and-Wednesday class is `24`. To end on a date instead, use `ends.type: "until"` with an `endDate` and skip the arithmetic.

The area is checked for a clash on the **first** occurrence only - the same rule the admin dashboard applies. Later occurrences are written without re-checking the court, so a series can land on a slot that is already held in a later week; read GET /v1/platform/areas/{areaId}/availability for the window first if that matters.

The response is the first occurrence, and for a recurring create it also carries `series.occurrencesCreated` - what this request actually wrote. Compare it with what you asked for: an occurrence at a club that is closed, or past its closing date, is skipped rather than failing the create. Read the rest of the series back with GET /v1/platform/classes filtered on the `recurrenceId` it carries.

post.description:
Enrols one customer in a class occurrence, with any guests they bring - the booking the club's own staff make when they add someone to a class. Every seat takes the class's time, club and price; capacity for the whole party, the class type's party size (`CLASS_PARTY_TOO_LARGE`), the class's booking policy, a waitlist entry the customer already holds (converted into this booking) and the "already on this class" check all apply exactly as they do in the admin portal. Identify the customer with `contactId` (resolve it via GET /v1/platform/contacts) or with an inline `customer` matched to a contact by email and created if new - exactly one of the two.

`quantity` counts the places, the customer's own included: `3` is the customer and two guests. The seats are sold as one order, so the guests' seats carry no contact, show the customer as who bought them, and are released with the customer's seat when it is cancelled.

Payment works as on POST /v1/platform/bookings: `paid` records the seats as settled against a payment method named after your API key (no gateway call), with your `reference` on each seat's payment and your `fee` shared over them; `unpaid` leaves them outstanding. `amount` is what the whole enrolment cost, shared over the seats in proportion to their price. With `unpaid` and no `amount`, the customer's seat is paid for the way the club's own staff would default it: a membership of the customer's that covers the class is used (one session is spent and nothing is owed), and otherwise the class price is recorded as owed; a guest's seat always owes the class price. With an API key that needs the customer named by `contactId`: an inline `customer` never spends a membership, and the class price is recorded as owed.

A full class, a cancelled one and one that has already run are refused; nothing here overrides them. Returns the customer's own seat, as POST /v1/platform/bookings returns a booking, with `classId`, `orderId` and `seatBookingIds` (every seat of the enrolment) set.

delete.description:
Retires a contact. Nothing is destroyed: the contact is archived, which drops them out of the contacts list and out of every search, while their transaction history stays intact - so the response is the contact itself, now with `type` `archived`, rather than an empty body. Archiving also releases everything they hold on the forward schedule - active memberships, bookings they organized, and bookings they are only a player on - and none of that is restored by un-archiving, which is done in 1club.

To preview the impact, `GET /v1/platform/memberships?contactId={id}` lists the memberships that will be cancelled, and `GET /v1/platform/bookings?contactId={id}` the bookings that will be. Neither is an exhaustive preview, so treat them as indicative: the bookings list matches only bookings the contact **organized** - never the ones they are an additional player on, which are released too - and it defaults to a **7-day** window, so pass `from` and `to` (up to 93 days per request, consecutive windows beyond that) to see further out.

A release can fail on an individual membership or booking without blocking the archive - the contact is retired either way, so a stuck booking cannot leave it active. That answers **409 `ARCHIVE_INCOMPLETE`** (not a 200) with the unreleased items in `details.outstanding`, precisely so the result is never cached against an `Idempotency-Key`: **repeat the same request to reconcile.** On an already archived contact the release runs again instead of short-circuiting, which is what makes the retry finish the job. A repeat call after a 200 is a no-op.

Needs its own `contacts:delete` scope for that reason; `contacts:write` alone cannot retire a member. Two contacts are refused rather than archived, because each needs a decision the call cannot make: a **staff member or owner** who can reach the admin portal (archiving would revoke that login - remove their access in 1club first); an **instructor** whose profile still has upcoming classes or recurring templates (reassign those first); and a contact **paying part of a split bill** on a future booking (settle that split first, since taking someone off a bill moves money and archiving moves none). An ordinary member with a portal login is *not* refused - that is most of the people worth archiving.

Without it such an archive is refused (409 `CANCELLATION_CHARGE_DECISION_REQUIRED`) and nothing changes. Unpaid bookings owe nothing either way unless it is `true`.

get.description:
Returns transactions for the organization associated with the API token, filtered by transaction creation time and ordered by `createdAt` descending, then by id. Each bound is an ISO date-time, or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` read as midnight UTC. `startDate` is inclusive and `endDate` is exclusive. When both are omitted, the window defaults to the last 24 hours (`endDate = now`, `startDate = now - 24h`); when only one is given, the other is derived from that same 24-hour span.

A single request may span at most 93 days. Cover a longer range in consecutive windows, passing the previous window's `endDate` as the next one's `startDate` - because the upper bound is exclusive, that chains without counting a boundary transaction twice.

Filtering by `contactId`, `bookingId` or `membershipId` lists that record's transactions. With one of those and no `startDate`/`endDate`, there is no window at all: every transaction of the contact, booking or membership comes back, newest first. Send a bound to window it as usual.

Note that this endpoint returns a bare array with no total - a full page (`limit` rows) means there are probably more, so keep advancing `offset` until a short page comes back.

Ordering is total (`createdAt` descending, then id), so `offset` paging is well defined for a fixed set of rows. It is not stable against concurrent writes: rows are ordered newest first, so a transaction created part-way through a walk lands on the first page and shifts every later row down by one, which can push an unread row past an `offset` already passed. Pass an explicit `endDate` in the past rather than relying on the `now` default - anything written after it falls outside the window and cannot shift the pages underneath you.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on transaction `createdAt`, as an ISO date-time or `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to `endDate - 24h`, or to no bound when filtering by contact, booking or membership.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on transaction `createdAt`, as an ISO date-time or `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to `now`, or to no bound when filtering by contact, booking or membership.

Removes a charge raised by mistake from the ledger. Only a charge nothing has happened to can be deleted: unpaid (`pending`, `overdue` or `failed`) or already `void`, and with no payment, invoice, Wallet entry, refund or other charge referring to it, and on no open order (`409 CHARGE_ON_OPEN_ORDER`) - anything else is refused with `409 TRANSACTION_HAS_RECORDS`, and should be voided instead. A paid charge is refused with `409 PAID_TRANSACTION_REQUIRES_REFUND`, and a settled or cancelled one with `409 CLOSED_TRANSACTION_NOT_DELETABLE`. An API key reaches only the charges of bookings it made through the API, as on a void.

When the charge was the last one of a pass that was never paid, the pass is cancelled with it, with its bookings still ahead; `releasedMembershipIds` names them. Deleting cannot be undone: to keep a record that the charge existed, void it.

Changes the website's name, theme behaviour and site-wide SEO defaults. Every field is optional; omitted fields are left alone.
`supportedLocales` and `defaultLocale` are **organization-level** and need the additional `organization:write` scope. They also decide which languages the member portal, the mobile app and outbound email offer, and they take effect immediately rather than on publish - so they are a separate grant from editing the draft. They are reachable here at all because they are what decides which localized URLs the website serves: a page or section translated into an unlisted locale has no URL to be served at and no `hreflang` alternate pointing to it. A `defaultLocale` outside `supportedLocales` is a 400.
Everything else in this body edits the **draft**, `seoSettings` included - it is stored in the site's settings, so a release carries it and the public site keeps serving the previously published values until you publish.
Deliberately cannot change the site's address (`slug`, `domain`), which website is the organization's default, or whether the site is switched on - those move a customer's public presence and are not side effects a content edit should have.

Unlike `seoSettings` this MERGES field by field, so setting the shape leaves the casing alone. An all-default style is stored as nothing, and the renderer falls back to `pill`.

Read this before writing a theme. It is the machine-readable counterpart to `/section-types`: that one says what may go IN a page, this one says how the site LOOKS. Tokens are added over time, so read it rather than hardcoding the values.
Two things worth knowing before you write anything. **Unset is the normal state** — every token falls back to the organization's branding or to a value derived from the tokens above it, so a good theme sets the fewest tokens it needs and leaves the rest inherited. And **the tokens are only coherent in combinations**, which is what `presets` are for: start from one and adjust two or three tokens, rather than composing 32 from scratch.

Overwriting a `branding` value is how a site quietly stops matching the rest of the customer's brand, so prefer leaving those alone unless asked.

put.description:
Merges a flat token patch into the site's theme, optionally on top of a named preset. Read `GET /theme-tokens` first for the tokens, their allowed values and the presets.
**This writes the draft**, like every other edit here — nothing a visitor sees changes until `POST /releases` publishes it. That is the point of tokens living on the website rather than on the organization's branding: a palette change is previewable, versioned in the release, and revertible.
Merges field by field, so setting the heading font leaves the palette alone. Send `null` for a token to return it to what it inherits — from the organization's branding, from another token, or from the platform default. That is the only way back once a value has been written; there is no "unset" string.
A `preset` is the exception to that merge: it REPLACES the look rather than adding to it. Every token any preset owns is cleared first, then the chosen preset's values are written. Otherwise switching from `night` to `editorial` would keep night's whole dark palette underneath and leave the site describing a hybrid nobody chose. Tokens no preset owns — a hand-picked brand colour — are untouched.
When `preset` and `tokens` are both sent the preset is applied first and the tokens land on top, so "use the editorial look but keep our heading font" is one call.
Every problem with a patch is reported at once rather than one at a time. Tokens are validated against the catalog: an unknown key, a value outside a token's options, a font the site cannot load, or a colour that is not a hex are all refused rather than stored — a colour CSS cannot parse does not fall back, it paints the surface transparent.

put.summary: Update the site header or footer
put.description:
The header and footer are site-level and render on every page. Config is merged into what is there, creating the slot if the site has none.
The link arrays (`navItems` on the header, `linkCategories`/`links` on the footer) **replace** rather than merge - read the current layout from `GET /v1/platform/website` and send the complete array, or you will drop the links you left out. Keep each link's `_id` when you send it back: translations are keyed on it, and a link without one gets a new id and loses its translations.
`translations` localizes the header or footer the way it does a page section, and like there it **replaces** the slot's whole locale map. A link is addressed by its `_id`, which `GET /v1/platform/website` returns on every item: `navItems.<_id>.label`, `navItems.<_id>.children.<_id>.label`, `linkCategories.<_id>.links.<_id>.label`.
